model: Bank FCFE at cost of equity (engine route): NI to ordinary shareholders less CET1 and associate retention, net debt zero, per ordinary share, USD flows bridged to a GBp quote

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case revenue path average (years 1-10); equity CAGR rejected (see warning); 3yr CAGRs are FY2022 IFRS17-restated -> FY2025 so the IFRS 17 step-change is excluded; 5yr CAGRs start from the FY2020 COVID/zero-rate trough and overstate
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (0.2-1.9%) diverges by far more than 30% from revenue (6.3-10.5%) and EPS (17-45%) CAGRs. Cause: $30bn+ of buy-backs FY22-FY25 plus a 50%+ payout keep ordinary equity flat while per-share earnings compound, and FY2020 is a rate/credit trough that inflates every 5yr CAGR. Neither series is a forward growth rate; the base case uses management's revenue target (positive growth rising to 5% in 2028).
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are null: bank OCF/FCF is meaningless (deposit and trading-balance flows). SBC is ~0.9% of revenue and stable, so the SBC adjustment does not distort growth. EPS is in USD per ordinary share (CSV eps column); the GBp quote is not used in any CAGR.

scenario_narratives.base: HSBC delivers the bottom of its 17%+ RoTE target through 2028. Banking NII holds around $46bn as the structural hedge reinvests at higher yields while policy rates drift lower; wealth fees in Hong Kong and IWPB grow high single digits; the $1.8-2.0bn of simplification saves and Hang Seng synergies keep cost growth near 1-2%. ECL runs ~45bp in 2026 with Hong Kong CRE still bleeding, then normalises to 30-40bp. CET1 is held at ~14% and roughly 70-80% of earnings go out as the 50% dividend plus quarterly buy-backs. After 2028 returns fade to ~16% as the rate tailwind is competed away and trade-finance share continues to leak to Standard Chartered and Citi.
scenario_narratives.bull: The 19% RoTE (ex notables) printed in 1H26 is the new normal rather than a peak. Hong Kong's super-connector role and cross-border wealth flows drive Asia wealth and insurance growth; wholly-owned Hang Seng delivers the full $0.9bn synergy opportunity; UK ring-fencing reform ('Growth Allowance') frees capital and lending capacity; HK CRE losses are cleared through portfolio sales and ECL drops to ~30bp. Revenue grows 6-7% for three years and RoTE settles near 19%.
scenario_narratives.bear: The two concentrations bite together. Faster rate cuts across USD/HKD and GBP compress banking NII as the hedge rolls off, while a mainland China slowdown and tariff-driven trade contraction push Hong Kong CRE, mainland-linked corporate and trade exposures into a credit cycle: ECL near 1% of loans in year 2 and revenue down 2%. US-China sanctions friction raises compliance costs and constrains the cross-border model, and legacy litigation (Madoff/Herald appeals) recurs. Returns recover only to ~13% RoTE, roughly the pre-2022 franchise economics plus the simplification savings.

valuation_philosophy.summary: HSBC is valued as the cash its ordinary shareholders can actually take out: NI to ordinary (after AT1 coupons and the now-small NCI) less the CET1 needed to keep the ratio at ~14.1% as the balance sheet grows, less undistributed associate (BoCom/SAB) earnings, discounted at a 10.5% USD cost of equity. Deposits are funding, not debt, so net debt is zero and nothing is deducted after the flows. Value is computed per ordinary share in USD and bridged to pence sterling at spot GBPUSD so it is comparable to the LSE quote; the USD siblings are kept alongside.
key_risks_to_valuation: Hong Kong/mainland China CRE: $6.3bn stage-3 HK CRE at end-2025; a deeper cycle is the main driver of the bear case
Rate sensitivity: banking NII guidance is conditioned on mid-July 2026 market rates; the structural hedge tailwind reverses in a fast cutting cycle
US-China geopolitical/sanctions risk to the cross-border model
Notable items recur nearly every period (BoCom impairment/dilution, disposal losses on exits, litigation): the model's underlying margin assumes they average small
BoCom carrying value: the 2.0%-of-revenue associate retention charge is a judgment; full retention would lower value ~3%
FX: a GBp holder's value moves one-for-one with GBPUSD; a 5% stronger pound takes ~5% off every GBp figure here with no change in the USD business

Share count after 29-Sep-2026 relies on the TVR announcement read in the ADR build; a new buy-back announced with 3Q26 results (late Oct 2026) would lower it further (value-neutral per share under this method)

sanity_check_caveat.status: FALSE PASS -- scripts/sanity_check.py applies inputs.fx_rate in the quote->reporting direction (its own docstring) while dcf_engine.py defines fx_rate as model->quote (USD -> GBp = 75.5687). It therefore multiplies the GBp price by 75.57 instead of dividing, printing a 'price' of ~105,480, P/B ~114x and P/Sales ~332x, and a 10-year table of P/B 3,000-7,700x. Nothing crossed a trip threshold only because the thresholds are absolute multiples that the inflated history also inflates. Same systemic bug recorded in memory (sanity-check-fx-rate-direction-systemic-bug; BA.L fx=100 case); not fixed here because scripts/ changes need TDD + corpus recompute. Do not read the sanity_check block's multiples as real.

real_multiples_at_current_price.basis: price 1,395.8p / 75.5687 = USD per ordinary share; TTM EPS = NI to ordinary 24,218 / weighted basic 17,146; TNAV 160,652 and ordinary equity (196,682 - AT1 23,708 - NCI 399) over 17,142M issued shares. P/TNAV ~2.0x against a ~17% RoTE target and 10.5% CoE is consistent with a justified P/TNAV of (RoTE - g)/(CoE - g) = (17-3)/(10.5-3) = 1.9x, i.e. the market is pricing the target being met -- which is what the -9% weighted upside says.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 959.3-1,610.0p; parity cross-checked against the NYSE HSBC ADS (5:1) at GBPUSD=X
data_sources.financials: HSBC Holdings Annual Reports FY2014-FY2025 and Interim Reports H1-2015 to H1-2026 (research/HSBA.L/Extracted), HSBA.L_Metrics.csv and kpis (incl. IFRS 17 restated FY2022 comparatives); 2026 Interim Report (HSBA.L_Quarterly_Q2-2026.txt) for 1H26 flows, capital and share counts; Total Voting Rights 2026-09-30 for the post-buy-back issued count

inputs.share_count_basis: ORDINARY SHARES, fully diluted, millions (HSBA.L is the primary LSE line; 1 ordinary share = 1/5 of a NYSE ADS and 1 HK share). 17,184M in issue at 30-Jun-2026 (1H26 balance sheet, HSBA.L_Quarterly_Q2-2026.txt), less 48.66M cancelled in the $1bn buy-back that concluded 2026-09-26 = ~17,142M (Total Voting Rights announcement 2026-09-30, read in the HSBC ADR build; not in HSBA.L/Extracted), plus 99M dilutive potential ordinary shares (1H26 EPS note: diluted 17,245M vs basic 17,146M weighted, line 6865-6867) = 17,241M. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed inside the flow and buy-backs are the distribution of the flow, value-neutral per share.
inputs.sbc_source: TTM to 2026-06-30: FY2025 'Share-based payment expense' 621 (HSBA.L_Annual_FY2025.txt:21852) - 1H25 315 + 1H26 319 (HSBA.L_Quarterly_Q2-2026.txt:6641). Bank: last_fcf is NI to ordinary shareholders TTM (FY25 21,102 - 1H25 11,510 + 1H26 14,626 = 24,218); reported_fcf = NI + SBC for auditability. Equity-award taxes: not separately disclosed, nil assumed.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 buy-backs $9,091m (kpis ShareRepurchases); 1H26 nil (paused Jan-2026 for the Hang Seng privatisation); up to $1bn announced 2026-08-04 and completed 2026-09-26. Dividends paid on ordinary shares FY2025 $11,581m (HSBA.L_Annual_FY2025.txt:22180); FY2025 DPS $0.75. Payout target 50% of EPS ex material notable items, buy-backs resuming only as CET1 is restored inside 14-14.5%.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows are USD (HSBC's reporting currency); the LSE quote is pence sterling. fx_rate converts model to quote: 1 USD = 100 / GBPUSD 1.3233 = 75.5687 GBp (Yahoo GBPUSD=X, 2026-10-09 21:29 UTC). The engine multiplies every USD per-ordinary-share figure by it, so canonical intrinsic_value, weighted_iv and entry_price are in GBp and comparable to current_price; *_usd siblings hold the model-currency figures. Parity check 2026-10-09 closes: HSBA.L 1,395.8p x 1.3233 / 100 x 5 = $92.35 per ADS-equivalent vs NYSE HSBC ADS $92.98, 0.7% apart; the 5:1 ADS ratio and the GBp bridge hold.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T15:49:18Z LSE regular close (Yahoo Finance chart API; 2026-10-10 is a Saturday, no later print)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity 10.5% built in USD because the flows are USD (the GBp quote is bridged at spot, not discounted at a GBP rate): 10y UST ~4.2% + beta ~1.05 x 5.25% ERP = ~9.7%, plus ~0.75pp for Hong Kong/mainland China earnings concentration and US-China sanctions/geopolitical exposure that US peers (WFC/USB at 10.0%) do not carry. Same rate as the HSBC ADR valuation of the same equity (2026-10-04) and TFC. One rate across all three scenarios; risk is carried in the bear path and its 25% weight.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable: the bank FCFE flow is after all operating costs including occupancy and IFRS-16 depreciation/interest; no lease adjustment (lease liabilities $3.3bn, HSBA.L_Annual_FY2025.txt:26943, are operating funding).
inputs.nci_treatment: Inside the flow. 'ebitda' = PBT + SBC - pre-tax equivalent of (AT1 coupons + NCI), so the flow is NI to ORDINARY shareholders. TTM AT1 coupons 1,269 (FY25 1,183 at :5933 - 1H25 547 + 1H26 633 at Q2-2026:1797); NCI 524 (FY25 846 - 1H25 384 + 1H26 62). NCI collapses from 2026 because the $13.7bn Hang Seng privatisation (completed 26-Jan-2026) derecognised $7.0bn of NCI (balance 7,441 -> 399, Q2-2026:2125); AT1 coupons rise ~$0.1-0.2bn on $4.0bn issued in 1H26 less $1.0bn redeemed (Q2-2026:6657,6661; AT1 par 20,716 -> 23,708). AT1 par and NCI are NOT deducted again in a bridge: shareholders_equity in the CSV (196,682) includes both, so a reader comparing to book must strip 23,708 AT1 and 399 NCI to get ordinary equity 172,575 / tangible 160,652.
inputs.notes: MODEL: FCFE at cost of equity through the component engine with net_debt = 0 -- the house method for large banks (WFC, USB, TFC, HBAN, NAB.AX) and the method used for the HSBC NYSE ADR line of this same equity on 2026-10-04. SKILL.md routes banks to residual income on tangible book; FCFE-at-CoE with a CET1-retention charge is the same economics (value = TCE + PV of returns above CoE) expressed as distributable cash. Deposits ($1.8tn customer accounts) are operating funding, not debt; OCF is meaningless for a bank (CSV OCF swings -21bn to +182bn) so total_debt is NULL in core_metrics by design and FCF CAGRs are not computed. ENGINE MAPPING: revenue = net operating income before ECL (CSV definition); TTM to 2026-06-30 = FY25 68,274 - 1H25 34,122 + 1H26 37,742 = 71,894. 'ebitda' = PBT 33,619 (29,907 - 15,810 + 19,522) + SBC 625 - (AT1 1,269 + NCI 524)/(1 - 22.63%) 2,317 = 31,927 = 44.4% of revenue. FY0 check: (31,927 - 625) x (1 - 22.63%) = 24,218 = NI to ordinary. TTM is depressed by ~$2.5bn pre-tax of notable items (H2-25 Madoff/Herald $1.1bn provision, BoCom $1.0bn impairment in 1H25 is outside the TTM window, restructuring, disposal losses; 1H26 Malta HFS loss, restructuring, UK Life FX recycling), so year 1 steps up to the underlying level. 'capex' = (a) CET1 retention to hold CET1/revenue at 1.7761 (reported CET1 127,692 at 30-Jun-2026, Q2-2026:5492, 14.1% of RWA 906,417) as revenue grows: 177.61 x g/(1+g), floored at zero; plus (b) 2.0% of revenue for undistributed associate earnings (share of associates ~$3bn/yr, mostly BoCom and Saudi Awwal Bank; BoCom pays ~30%, so ~$1.8bn/yr is retained in entities HSBC cannot distribute from). CET1 14.1% sits inside the 14-14.5% target, so NO excess-capital credit in the bridge. D&A = 0 (inside opex). IFRS 17: FY2022 and earlier are pre-IFRS 17; the 3yr CAGRs use the restated FY2022 comparatives (kpis Revenue_IFRS17Restated 50,620, NetIncome_IFRS17Restated 14,346), and the projection is anchored on the post-IFRS17 TTM so the step-change never enters a growth rate. DRIVER PATHS: identical to the HSBC ADR valuation of 2026-10-04 by deliberate choice -- same company, same filings, no new disclosure between the two dates (3Q26 results are due late October 2026); two inconsistent views of one equity would be an error, not independence. What IS this ticker's own: the GBp price, the GBPUSD bridge, the per-ordinary-share basis (17,241M diluted vs 3,449M ADS), the CET1 anchor read as reported (127,692) rather than back-solved from the ratio (127,805), and every citation into HSBA.L's own Extracted files. CROSS-CHECK: the ADR's weighted IV $84.20/ADS on 2026-10-02 = $16.84 per ordinary share = ~1,273p at today's GBPUSD; this build should land within a few pence of that, the residual being the CET1 anchor and the 1H26-basis dilutive count. Yahoo HSBA.L print 2026-10-09 15:49Z is the LSE close (15:30Z + closing auction); the share fell ~5% on 2026-10-01 and a further ~5% over 7-9 Oct with no company announcement identified.

bear.margin_rationale: Global rate cuts reverse the structural-hedge tailwind (NII down), a HK/China CRE and trade-tariff credit cycle takes ECL to ~1% of loans in year 2 (~$5.5bn above base), and legacy litigation recurs. Recovery only to 42% margin: terminal RoTE ~13%, the pre-2022 franchise economics with partial credit for simplification. CET1 retention floored at zero in the year-2 contraction (regulators would not permit a capital release in a credit cycle).

base.growth_rationale: Year 1 (Jul-26 to Jun-27) 5.5%: H2-26 ~$37bn (banking NII guided at least $46bn for 2026 vs $22.9bn in 1H26) plus H1-27 ~$39bn against a TTM depressed by H2-25 notable-item revenue losses. Then management's 2026-28 target of growth rising to 5% in 2028 (HSBA.L_Annual_FY2025.txt:253-257, reaffirmed Q2-2026:315-317), fading to 3% nominal.
base.margin_rationale: Year 1 48.0% gives NI to ordinary ~$27.5bn = ~17% RoTE on ~$163bn average tangible equity (1H26 average 162,713), the bottom of the 17%+ 2026-28 target (1H26 ran 19.1% ex notables, but H2 carries heavier costs and ECL guided ~45bp for 2026). Margin edges up to 49% as $1.8-2.0bn simplification saves and Hang Seng synergies meet ~1% cost growth, then fades to 48% as the structural-hedge tailwind ends and ECL normalises at 30-40bp. Terminal RoTE ~16%.
base.capex_rationale: CET1 retention 177.61 x g/(1+g) holding CET1 at 14.1% of RWA as revenue grows, plus 2.0% of revenue undistributed associate (BoCom/SAB) earnings. Implied distribution ratio ~69% in year 1 and ~80% at terminal, in line with the 50% dividend plus buy-backs.
base.tax_rationale: TTM ETR 22.63% (FY25 22.7%, 1H26 21.5%); 23% reflects UK bank surcharge, HK 16.5%, Pillar Two top-ups.

bull.margin_rationale: 1H26's 19% RoTE ex notables proves durable: wealth fees compound (Asia net new invested assets $80bn in 2025), rates stay higher for longer, HK CRE losses roll off and ECL returns to ~30bp, Hang Seng synergies ($0.5bn + $0.4bn) land in full. RoTE ~18.5-19.5% sustained.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25% (up from the 15% default): earnings rest on one geography (Hong Kong/mainland China ~half of profit) with live CRE stress and US-China sanctions exposure, and NII is explicitly rate-dependent. Base 50%: guidance has been met or raised twice in 2026. Bull 25% (down from 35%): 1H26 RoTE is already above target, so the bull needs peak-cycle returns to persist rather than improve. Same weighting as the HSBC ADR line of this equity.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
